problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ of the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n-1}(n-1)!}=x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\cdot 1}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{{2}^{2}\cdot 2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{{2}^{3}\cdot 3!}+⋯\,.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n)!}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n)!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{2n+3}}{(2n+2)!}\cdot \frac{(2n)!}{{x}^{2n+1}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{2}(2n)!}{(2n+2)!}| \\  & =|{x}^{2}|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(2n)!}{(2n+2)!} \\  & ={x}^{2}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(2n)!}{(2n)!(2n+1)(2n+2)} \\  & ={x}^{2}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(2n+1)(2n+2)} \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty ,$ and the interval of convergence is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
